A SQL predicate/double read or wrapper cannot certify that the process generation is unchanged through the actual native signal. No alternate mechanism was authorized or introduced.

SPEC_SOURCE.text: Deployment identity stored in a backup is insufficient for clone isolation. Trusted host orchestration keeps clone/restore NOT_READY and inaccessible to operational logins until explicit REINCARNATION rotates the server's incarnation marker, disables restored offline identities and invalidates copied bindings. Incarnation readiness and expected endpoint/incarnation are independent deployment prerequisites. This is an operational boundary against copied deployments, not protection from a hostile host/database administrator.

NOT_READY/READY is host-governed. Clone/restore starts NOT_READY before exposure: block operational network/authentication, disable restored offline logins, explicit REINCARNATION with fresh identity governed outside ordinary DB backup, rotate private DB incarnation marker, invalidate copied headers, verify history/catalog/watchdog, then enable freshly reviewed identities/bindings. Old identities tombstoned/disabled, never rebound. Existing credential/later effects -> manual review, no regeneration. READY requires host incarnation/private marker agreement. Client expected endpoint/incarnation from approved deployment config, never copied header. DB cannot detect undeclared clone if trusted host admin bypasses procedure; hostile-admin protection not claimed. Same names/OIDs/content copied fixture must deny while NOT_READY and after new incarnation. Normal restart retains incarnation and ownership.

Provision private incarnation/policy/receipt key/watchdog -> owners/controls/wrappers -> four fresh logins/header/initial states/ACLs -> activation -> matching launcher. Service password delivery distinct from command TTY. OID/name/incarnation checks/tombstones/no rebinding. Dedicated pools discard stale-incarnation sessions. No admin SET ROLE shortcut or impossible hostile-superuser session-authorization detection claim.

Decode/validate all29 policy fields and recompute SHA-256 of the complete canonical policy; reject missing/duplicate/mismatched policy, invalid bounds or unapproved version. Capture issued_at from authoritative pg_catalog.clock_timestamp(), represented as the existing signed int8 epoch-microsecond instant. Derive expires_at = issued_at + preflight_receipt_ttl microseconds using exact checked integer-microsecond arithmetic; require representable finite instants and expires_at > issued_at, without rounding, clamping, overflow, fallback or hidden hard-coded TTL. Caller MUST NOT supply issued_at or expires_at as issuance inputs. Their later presence inside the authenticated receipt is transport of Q's server-derived values, not caller authority. Once issued, the receipt's issued_at/expires_at/policy digest remain immutable and covered by its HMAC. Validity is issued_at <= database_now < expires_at, with database_now freshly read from pg_catalog.clock_timestamp(); equality at expiry is expired. Transaction-start time, client/JVM clocks and session timeout settings are not expiry authority. Other binding/state/deadline checks remain independent and may deny earlier; they do not rewrite the receipt expiration formula.

G3F.3B.1 single-rule consumption: S01 invokes Q's AUDITOR/sentinel issuance route, which uses exactly21.2 PREFLIGHT_EXPIRY_DERIVATION. S13 invokes Q's EXECUTOR validation route with the original nonempty receipt; Q verifies framing/current ACTIVE-key HMAC and exact scope, then rederives expires_at from the original authenticated issued_at and the same exact policy_version/digest/TTL. Require exact encoded expiry equality and fresh database-time validity, then repeat live readiness checks. On this route Q returns the original validated receipt bytes unchanged, never a new issued_at/expiry or renewed MAC. S13 repeats database-time validity immediately before creating or confirming claim ownership and before returning its claim receipt. Expired/future-issued/malformed/policy-drift receipts fail closed with existing sanitized diagnostics and no new claim/confirmation effect. Lost-ack/idempotent S13 retry has the same receipt checks; even an otherwise matching execution cannot replay an expired receipt to restore validity. A fresh eligible S01 issuance is a separate operation and never revives old receipt bytes, renews existing execution deadlines or restores delivery/admission authority. S01/Q/S13 accept no caller-selected duration, expiry, policy fallback or alternate rule; SQL signatures and owner/column grants remain unchanged.

Provisioning is explicit, separate from V043, atomic and governed by a prior independent administrative approval. One transaction inserts the new policy row and, where applicable, atomically establishes its existing approved references under the existing lifecycle/control locks. It validates the complete row/reference set before commit. No in-place policy UPDATE/DELETE, upsert that overwrites a version, default insertion, unapproved binding mutation or reuse of an existing version is permitted. Operational exclusion prevents exposure of tentative/intermediate state. Validation/query/commit uncertainty denies activation until durable committed state and audit evidence are independently reconciled; no retry may replace values under the same version.
